# Paper plan (generated by Section 9 of this run)

Main text (ACL long paper, 8 pages):
1. Introduction: pass@k far beyond the sampled n is forecast routinely; the quadratic horizon, the error floor at the benchmark sizes in use, certification near 2n, and one practical rule (attempts per problem buy more than problems).
2. Setting and Theorem 1. (A) the quadratic horizon 2E_n(x^k); (B) the doubling estimator and its certificate for k < 2n; (C) the finite-sample lower bound. Figure: F1_population_horizon.
3. Certified estimation stops near 2n (C1, E7). Figure: F20_certified_horizon_vs_m; the worst-case two-point bound reaches 0.1 at t = 11.2 to 34 (LP certifies up to 2.5).
4. What any estimator can achieve on real count laws (E10), read as an error floor at a realistic benchmark size. Figures: F27_error_floor_and_stability, F29_error_bracket_realistic_m, F24_problems_needed_any_estimator, F26_bound_tightness_and_stability, F28_likelihood_ratio_simulation. Tables: T19_error_floor_realistic_m, T22_error_bracket_realistic_m, T20_floor_vs_problems_needed_stability, T15c_problems_needed_fixed_k, T17_upper_vs_lower_bound, T21_likelihood_ratio_simulation.
   - floor: m = 1,319: k=2n 0.001-0.011 (above 0.05 for 0/10), k=4n 0.002-0.044 (above 0.05 for 0/10), k=8n 0.002-0.122 (above 0.05 for 5/10), k=16n 0.003-0.205 (above 0.05 for 7/10), k=32n 0.004-0.242 (above 0.05 for 7/10), k=64n 0.005-0.310 (above 0.05 for 7/10); at k=16n the floor exceeds 0.05 for 7/10 count laws (0.084 to 0.205)

5. Ground truth on Monkey Business (C5b-C5d). Figure: F23_family_choice_ground_truth. Table: T14b_monkey_business_family_choice.
   - bands: PASS (9/9 configurations); backtest: NOT SUPPORTED (2/6 informative streams); flip: NOT SUPPORTED (0/6 informative streams)
6. Related work (Singh and Singh 2026; Yang, Zhang and Chen 2026; Kazdan et al. 2025; Brown et al. 2024; Schaeffer et al. 2025; Newman and Rivlin 1976; Efron and Thisted 1976; Orlitsky, Suresh and Wu 2016).
7. Limitations (from this run):
   - The E10 bound is local: it covers estimators that must be accurate at every distribution whose count law is within h(m) of the real one, not estimators allowed to assume a parametric family.
   - At +-0.05 the bound is silent for GSM8K L3-8B-I and GSM8K L3-70B-I, where pass@k is already close to 1.
   - The likelihood-ratio check (T17, T21, T22) is made at the observed distributions only, not uniformly over the neighbourhood that the lower bound covers, and its alternatives live on a support grid.
   - The problems needed at k = 16n depends on which problems are in the benchmark: up to a factor of 1,200 between the 10th and 90th percentiles over resamples (T18); the error floor at m = 1,319 varies by a factor of at most 2.2 on the same resamples (T20).
   - Three count laws were resampled (T18, T20); the stability of the other seven is not measured.
   - The count laws come from 2024 models (Monkey Business) and from Qwen2.5 0.5B/1.5B; no current reasoning model is included.
   - Inside the sampled range the certified estimator is less accurate than the best forecaster: mean absolute error at k = 48 of 0.0364 against 0.0107 for the base model (best forecaster: power law); 0.0174 against 0.0087 for the instruct model (best forecaster: power law).
   - A3 fails for the instruct model (grader disagreement above 2%), so p_i there is a verifier-acceptance probability.
   - Pre-registered claims that the data did not support: C3 (retired); C5c on Monkey Business; C5d on Monkey Business.
